water: Released law. The runoff ratio Q/P falls exponentially with aridity φ = PET/P. The base of that exponential is 3.73 + δ: where rain falls in the cool season (δ < 0, out of phase with evaporation) runoff falls off more slowly, and snow (f_s) raises it. Adding soil storage S gained only 0.003 of frozen-set R², under the 0.01 margin, so the ratchet left it out. WaterSim's simplest strong belief is shorter still: Q/P ≈ 0.34 / φ.
fire: Released law. log₁₀ of tomorrow's new area is −0.56 / P: small fires grow a little, every fire with more than a few km of perimeter is predicted to add about 0.5-1 km² a day. Every law that let growth keep rising with perimeter, the way FireSim's fires do, made the real dev fire-days worse, so the ratchet stopped here. FireSim's own belief is G ≈ (0.32 P)^1.6 km²/day, with wind and dry fuel adding to it: on the real exam that runs a median 36 times too fast.
grid_inertia: Released law. Inertia is demand times about 6.6 s, minus 5.6 s for every unit of inverter-based share: E = D (6.60 − 5.62 s). It is GridSim's unit commitment in one line: wind, solar and imports displace synchronous machines one for one. The shape is right (rank correlation 0.975 on the exam, against 0.60 for 7 s × demand) but the level is not: GridSim's GB fleets commit about 4.5 s of inertia per MW of demand, real GB about 7, so the law reads real grids 33 % low.
grid_nadir: Released law. The frequency drop grows with the square of (ΔP + 2 GW) and falls slowly with inertia: Δf = (ΔP + 2)² · (5.3·10⁴ (E − 67))^−0.21. It comes from the generic-response physics (g1). GridPulse's dev-calibrated physics (g2, with Dynamic Containment) gave laws that scored higher on its own frozen set but read the four 2019 dev events 2.5-4.5 times worse, so the dev gate kept the g1 law. The simplest g2 belief is Δf ≈ 0.43 Hz per GW lost.
bldg: Released law. Annual energy per m² = 187 / 1.93^A + HDD × (2022 − Y): a small-home base load that halves with every extra 100 m², plus heating that grows with degree days and with the age of the house (1 kWh/m² per 1,000 K·day per year of age). Cooling degree days appear only in the largest rungs, which the ratchet rejected. BuildingSim at physics 1.4 (dev-fitted intensities) passed the dev gate; at 1.0 its homes used 1.4 times too much.
